theme: Canadian and Australian STR registries and datasets (Toronto, Vancouver, Montreal, Quebec CITQ, BC registry, Sydney NSW STRA register, Melbourne)

candidates.name: city-of-toronto-short-term-rentals-registration
candidates.what_it_holds: Git-scraping repo that pulls the City of Toronto Open Data 'Short Term Rentals Registration' dataset (all active STR registration numbers) daily at UTC midnight via GitHub Actions, and commits short-term-rental-registrations-data.csv each run, giving a de-facto point-in-time history of the registry as a commit log even though Toronto Open Data itself only serves the current snapshot.
candidates.why_useful: Directly fills gap #12 (city STR registration datasets: Toronto, Vancouver, Montreal/Quebec CITQ) with a genuinely point-in-time series (each git commit = a dated snapshot of registered-listing counts), which is rare — most municipal STR registries (including our existing Austin/Barcelona/Maui/NYC/CA holdings) are single current-state pulls, not vintaged. Toronto active-registration counts are a legal-supply proxy for a top-10 ABNB market.
candidates.time_coverage: Daily snapshots from repo creation (recent) forward; each commit is a dated point-in-time cut
candidates.size_hint: single CSV per commit, city registry size (thousands of rows)
candidates.license: repo has a LICENSE file (terms not confirmed in fetch); underlying data is City of Toronto Open Data (Open Government Licence – Toronto)
candidates.last_activity: actively updated (commit 11 hours before scout run, 14 Sep 2026)

candidates.name: TOHS-tool-rbc
candidates.what_it_holds: Daily GitHub Actions pipeline ('Rental Background Check') that normalizes and address-keys five Toronto/Ontario public datasets into JSON files partitioned by street-name letter (data/a.json … data/z.json, data/0-9.json): RentSafeTO apartment registry, Active Building Permits, the Short-Term Rental Registry, Multi-Tenant House Licences, and Planned Developments, plus the Ontario Landlord and Tenant Board Order Catalogue.
candidates.why_useful: A second, independently-built daily mirror of Toronto's STR registry (cross-check/backup for the RamVasuthevan repo above) plus adjacent housing-supply signals (building permits, multi-tenant licences) that bear on long-term vs short-term rental crossover economics for a major Canadian ABNB market (gap #12 and #13).
candidates.time_coverage: Daily since repo creation; historical depth uncertain
candidates.size_hint: JSON files, one per street-letter, city-scale row counts
candidates.license: MIT for pipeline code; data under Toronto/Ontario Open Government Licences (commercial use permitted with attribution)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: partially overlaps RamVasuthevan/city-of-toronto-short-term-rentals-registration for the STR-registry slice; adds permits/multi-tenant/LTB data not otherwise held

candidates.name: UPGo-McGill (org: Urban Politics and Governance lab, McGill)
candidates.what_it_holds: Academic research group's GitHub org with a family of repos on Canadian short-term-rental regulation and housing impacts: strr (R package/toolkit for cleaning and analyzing STR data, incl. commercial-operator and 'ghost hostel' detection, built around AirDNA property/daily files), citq-rapport-2024 (R code for a 2024 report specifically on Quebec's CITQ tourism-accommodation registry), bc-report-2024 (British Columbia STR/housing report code), ontario-report-2024 (Ontario STR/housing report code), montreal-finance-2022 (rental-housing financialization analysis), halifax-analysis, and mtl_landlords (Montreal landlord-data scraper). Repos hold analysis code (mostly R, MIT-licensed) and output figures rather than raw committed datasets; the underlying STR microdata is licensed AirDNA data not redistributed, but the CITQ/BC/Ontario report repos are the closest thing on GitHub to worked methodology specifically over the Quebec CITQ and BC STR registries named in gap #12.
candidates.why_useful: This is the one research group publicly building analysis pipelines exactly over Quebec CITQ and BC provincial STR registration data (gap #12) and Canadian STR commercial-operator/ghost-hostel detection (relevant to gap #9 supply and #2 realized occupancy proxies); their published PDF reports (linked from repos, e.g. via CMHC/McGill) may contain registry-level counts and trends even where the raw data itself is not redistributable, and the strr R package methodology (FREH, ghost-hostel, commercial-operator classification) is reusable on any listing-level panel we already hold (e.g. Inside Airbnb Canadian coverage) as an acquisition/classification method.
candidates.geography: Canada — Quebec (CITQ), British Columbia, Ontario/Toronto, Montreal, Halifax
candidates.time_coverage: Reports dated 2021-2024; strr package actively developed (422+ commits)
candidates.size_hint: code repos only (R scripts, figures); no large committed data files observed
candidates.license: MIT (code); underlying AirDNA data proprietary/licensed, not redistributed
candidates.last_activity: strr actively developed as of recent commits; report repos dated 2022-2024
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: no direct overlap; a methods/pointer complement to our Inside Airbnb Canadian-market gap, not a data duplicate

notes: WebSearch tool hit its session-wide 200-call budget after only 4 queries for this scout (shared across all concurrent scouts in this sweep) — remaining research used github.com/search?type=repositories fetched directly via WebFetch, which is not metered against that budget and worked well as a substitute; recommend other scouts try this fallback if they also hit the WebSearch cap. Direct GitHub full-text search for 'CITQ' and for 'STRA register NSW'/'STRA register data australia' returned zero or irrelevant hits, confirming these registries have essentially no GitHub presence outside the UPGo-McGill academic repos found here (no scraper/mirror of the actual NSW STRA register or the CITQ open-data extract exists on GitHub as far as this pass could tell). No usable GitHub hits at all for Sydney NSW STRA or Melbourne short-stay beyond generic Airbnb-price-prediction notebooks that don't touch registry data — this looks like a genuine hole (gap #12) worth flagging to a human for a direct Socrata/CKAN check of data.nsw.gov.au and data.vic.gov.au rather than further GitHub search. UPGo-McGill (McGill Urban Politics and Governance lab) is the standout find: an active academic group publishing STR regulatory analysis specifically over CITQ (Quebec), BC, and Ontario registries, plus a reusable `strr` R package for commercial-operator/ghost-hostel/FREH classification — none of their report repos' raw data contents could be confirmed without an authenticated read (README fetch via raw.githubusercontent.com 404'd, suggesting default branch may not be 'main'), so a follow-up with `gh repo view`/`gh api` on these five repos is the natural next step for whichever agent has gh search budget.
